product: Kaji No.7 — one chef's knife, sold direct
designChallenge: Deliberately the smallest scenario on the list, built because five of the six rounds before it were cut off mid-work and a truncated build teaches nothing. One product, one page, no grid, no catalogue, no filtering — so the entire budget lands on the thing every recent verdict says is missing: whether the subject is obtained and treated rather than constructed, whether the page moves because the material moves, and whether footage was searched for at all. A single-product page has nowhere to hide. There is no second column to fill and no grid whose repetition can pass for structure; if the knife is not shown being made, held, and used, the page is a spec sheet with a serif headline. Material is unusually well covered: forging, quenching, grinding sparks, water stones, and food being cut are among the most filmed processes in the free archives, and a blade is a single rigid object — the easiest possible subject for a turntable sequence, a depth pass, or a macro crop that survives being scrubbed. What to read off it: is there footage; is the blade the same blade in every frame; does anything change across a section other than opacity; and does the page make you want the object, which for a £280 knife is the only question that matters.
prompt: This is the page for the Kaji No.7, a chef's knife made by one smith and sold direct for £280. A buyer is deciding between this and a good factory knife at a fifth of the price. Redesign the page.
promptContentOnly: This is the page for the Kaji No.7, a chef's knife made by one smith and sold direct for £280. A buyer is deciding between this and a good factory knife at a fifth of the price, so the page has to make the difference visible rather than asserted. Design and build that page.
preserve: The price, the two handle options with their price difference, and which is in stock
Every specification: blade length, total length, weight, steel, hardness, and the bevel angle
The making statement — one smith, the number made per month, and the current lead time
The care facts, including that the steel is not stainless and will patina, and must not go in a dishwasher
The sharpening service offer and what it costs after the first free year
Both owner notes with their names and how long they have had the knife
The returns statement — 30 days unused, and the lifetime guarantee against a failure of the maker's work
